title: Inventory Value appears in the reports navigation under the Parts group
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (the report reuses it and adds no new permission — Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Your role has the ordinary reports access.
steps: 1. Open the reports navigation.
2. Look inside the Parts group of reports.
3. Click the "Inventory Value" entry.
expected: 1. The reports navigation lists a report labeled "Inventory Value" under the Parts group.
2. Clicking it opens the Inventory Value report.
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Inventory Value report specification version 4 (S1-R1).

title: One row per in-stock part at the selected locations valued at the resolved date
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Several ZZAUTOTEST parts with positive on-hand quantity exist at your active location.
steps: 1. Open the Inventory Value report.
2. Compare the rows shown to the in-stock parts at the selected location(s).
3. Note the date range in the toolbar and which date the values represent.
expected: 1. The report shows one row for each in-stock part at the selected location(s).

2. The values are valued as of the resolved date (the current stock for a range reaching today, or the closest recorded nightly snapshot for an earlier date — see the IV — As-of Date & Snapshots cases).
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Inventory Value report specification version 4 (S1-R2, S1-R6).

title: The report is server-paginated: one page of rows at a time
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. The selected location(s) hold more in-stock parts than fit on one page (seed ZZAUTOTEST parts if needed).
steps: 1. Open the Inventory Value report and scroll to the bottom of the rows, then keep scrolling so further rows load.
2. Watch that new rows keep arriving as you scroll rather than all of them being present at once.
3. After scrolling well down the list, change a server-side filter (for example select a Category), then look at where the list starts.
4. Repeat with a part search and with a sort change.
expected: 1. The server returns one page of rows at a time rather than the whole list at once; further rows keep arriving as you scroll to the bottom.
2. Changing any server-side filter (Date, Location, Category, Vendor), the part search, or the sort returns the FIRST page of the new result set - the list jumps back to the top.

3. Note for the tester: on the build tested there were no numbered page controls on the screen - the rows loaded as you scrolled. That is a difference from the specification, which asks for the reports suite's standard page controls. Record what you see and carry on.
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Inventory Value report specification version 4 (S1-R8).
Last checked against build v3.4.1-3d03023 on 8/4/2026.

title: No qualifying parts, day or location: the no-data message shows and no totals
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.

2. Three causes can be produced: (a) a location you can access holds no in-stock parts, (b) a past range ends entirely before nightly recording began (or its covered dates were pruned by retention), (c) the filters can be set so nothing qualifies.
steps: 1. Scope the report to the empty location and read the data area.
2. Select a Custom range ending before nightly recording began and read the data area and the bottom of the report.
3. Set the filters so nothing qualifies and re-read.
expected: 1. In every case the report shows the standard reports no-data message "Empty bays, endless possibilities. Get Going!" instead of rows.
2. No totals row is shown in any of the cases.
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Inventory Value report specification version 4 (S1-N2, S4-N1, S5-N1, S7-N2).
Last checked against build v3.4.1-3d03023 on 8/4/2026.

title: A part appears only if not a core charge and on-hand quantity is above zero
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.

2. ZZAUTOTEST parts exist at your active location: a normal part with positive on-hand quantity, a core-charge part with a positive quantity, a part with exactly zero on-hand quantity, and (if producible) one with a negative on-hand quantity.
steps: 1. Open the Inventory Value report scoped to the location.
2. Look for the normal in-stock part.
3. Search for the core-charge part, the zero-quantity part, and the negative-quantity part by part number; check the totals row.
expected: 1. The normal, positive-quantity, non-core part appears as one row.
2. The core-charge part is never listed — even with a positive quantity — and its value is not counted in the totals row.
3. The zero-quantity and negative-quantity parts are not listed — only quantities greater than zero are valued.
4. Only parts meeting BOTH conditions — not a core charge, and on-hand quantity greater than zero — are listed.
5. A part that has sat without movement for a long time still appears and is still counted — there is no dead-stock exclusion; how long stock has sat makes no difference.
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Inventory Value report specification version 4 (S2-R1, S2-R2, S2-N1, S2-N2).
Last checked against build v3.4.1-3d03023 on 8/4/2026.

title: A part stocked at two selected locations shows as two rows; never merged
permissions_required: A user with access to at least two locations and the inventory-reports permission.
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser as a user with access to at least two locations.
2. The same ZZAUTOTEST part is in stock (positive quantity) at two of those locations.
steps: 1. Open the Inventory Value report and select both locations in the Location filter.
2. Search for the part and count its rows.
expected: 1. The part appears twice — one row per location, each with that location's own quantity and values.
2. The rows are NOT merged into one combined row; this is the documented v1 behavior.
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Inventory Value report specification version 4 (S2-R3).

title: There is no dead-stock exclusion - a slow-moving part still appears
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.

steps: 1. Open the Inventory Value report scoped to the location.

expected: 1. The long-sitting part appears and its value is counted — every part currently holding positive, non-core stock contributes to the on-hand value, however long it has sat.
